messages:
maria: Heads-up — saw a perf regression on qwen2.5 in our multilingual bench. Latency p50 up ~22% for zh/ja inputs compared to en. Profiling points to the kernel selector choosing a fallback matmul kernel and the batcher frequently breaking into tiny batches.

raj: ugh, any logs? is this after the tokenizer changes? :thinking:

maria: Not the recent tokenizer patch — this regressed on the nightly model variant change. attaching the rough profiler excerpt below (trimmed).
```
kernel_selector: model=qwen2.5 size=384 seq=96 auto_pick=ON selected=matmul_small reason=heuristic_threshold
kernel_perf: matmul_small latency=1.8ms matmul_fast latency=0.9ms
batcher: incoming_rate spikes -> small_batch_path triggered (threshold=16 tokens)
kv_cache: misses_per_request=0.12 increase_from_baseline=3x
```

olivia: interesting — seq=96 for zh/ja? looks like tokenizer producing many short tokens or tokenizer splitting differently which increases effective batch fragmentation. can you share tokenization examples?

maria: yes — short sample:
- en: "Hello world" -> [Hello, world] (2 toks)
- zh: "你好世界" -> [你, 好, 世界] (3 toks) but token lengths smaller and more prefix overlap. also noticed a spike in early-stop KV cache reuse.

daniel: spike in KV cache misses is suspicious. if the runtime sees lots of sub-token flushes it may not reuse cached prefix keys, causing extra matmul shapes and kernel selector confusion. can you dump the exact shape stream?

maria: pasted relevant snippet (from debug run):
```
request 1: seq_len=12 kv_prefix=8 cache_hit=false selected_kernel=matmul_small
request 2: seq_len=8 kv_prefix=8 cache_hit=true selected_kernel=matmul_fast
request 3: seq_len=14 kv_prefix=8 cache_hit=false selected_kernel=matmul_small
```

jie: quick hypothesis: batching heuristic uses token-count thresholds tuned on en distributions; for multilang short-token-heavy inputs it fragments batches and the kernel chooser sees many small outliers so it picks the safe small kernel. two ways to test: 1) tune batcher to prefer slightly larger aggregate token windows, 2) add a kernel-selection override for certain token-size distribution shapes.

raj: can we reproduce with the repro script? which flags?

jie: run: `./perf/repro.sh --model qwen2.5 --lang zh --seq-dist short --profile kernel,kv,batcher` will produce the same stream. I also pushed a small batching heuristic tweak branch `batcher/soft-window` that delays small-batch fallback by 5ms to allow more aggregation.

maria: tried the branch locally — p50 back down ~12% (not fully to baseline). KV misses down from 0.12 -> 0.03. kernel selector still chooses matmul_small ~25% less. logs:
```
kernel_selector: seq=12 avg_token=2.1 selected=matmul_fast (after batch window=+5ms)
batcher: small_path avoided x78% of runs
kv_cache: misses_per_request=0.03
```

olivia: nice. sounds like two orthogonal issues: tokenizer distribution + overly conservative kernel thresholds. long-term: we should add an adaptive kernel threshold that learns per-model-per-lang distributions (or at least per-token-size quartiles). short-term: ship the batching soft-window and a config tweak to kernel thresholds for qwen2.5 multilingual buckets.

daniel: agree. also add a metric to trace kernel-switch frequency per-route so we can alert when it spikes. I can wire that into console dashboards.

infra-bot: deploy queued: batcher/soft-window -> canary on ded-cluster-3 at 1972468050 by jie.

maria: canary numbers after 10k requests on ded-cluster-3: p50 = baseline * 1.03 (good), p95 improved too, cost per-token ~ -2.1%. leaving canary running for 1h, will report back. :thumbsup:

raj: great. next actions: 1) merge soft-window, 2) create a kernel-threshold config for qwen2.5 multilingual that we can tweak remotely, 3) add kernel-switch metric. assigning to jie + daniel.

maria: thanks team — filing a short postmortem after canary.
